mainTopic: The story of רב אויא missing רב יוסף's Shabbat lecture (eating before מוסף, and praying before the צבור), the final הלכה on eating before מוסף and מנחה, and the short prayer of רבי נחוניא בן הקנה when entering and leaving the בית המדרש.
overview: The amud opens with a story. רב אויא missed רב יוסף's lecture, and אביי questions him so everyone can see he meant no disrespect. Along the way they discuss eating before מוסף and davening before the צבור, and the גמרא rules that the הלכה follows neither רב הונא nor רבי יהושע בן לוי on eating before davening. A משנה then tells of the short prayer רבי נחוניא בן הקנה said when entering and leaving the בית המדרש, and a ברייתא gives its full words. Next come two sickbed stories: רבי אליעזר teaches his students paths to עולם הבא, and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי cries in fear of judgment and blesses his students with יראת שמים. A new משנה follows about how much of שמונה עשרה one must say, along with prayer in danger and facing the בית המקדש. The גמרא asks what the eighteen ברכות correspond to, discusses how far to bow, and explains that the nineteenth ברכה, ברכת המינים, was added in יבנה by שמואל הקטן. The story of what happened when he later forgot it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב אויא misses the lecture
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא was sick and missed רב יוסף's lecture. The next day, אביי wants to calm רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא was weak and did not come to רב יוסף's lecture. The next day, when he came, אביי wanted to put רב יוסף's mind at ease.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a story and sets up the conversation that follows. אביי is about to question רב אויא in front of רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Missing your רבי's lecture could look like disrespect. אביי's questions are meant to show that רב אויא had a real reason. The story also teaches הלכות about davening and eating.

keyTerms.meaning: the public lecture, usually given on Shabbat
to put his mind at ease, to calm him

phrases.english: Rav Avya was weak
and did not come to Rav Yosef's lecture.
The next day, when he came,

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא אַבָּיֵי לְאַנּוֹחֵי דַּעְתֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף.
phrases.english: Abaye wanted to put Rav Yosef's mind at ease.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַוְיָא חֲלַשׁ וְלָא אֲתָא לְפִרְקָא דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: רב אויא missed the lecture, and אביי wants to calm רב יוסף.

steps.title: אביי asks why he missed the lecture
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב אויא why he did not come.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Why did the master not come to the lecture?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a direct question so that רב אויא can explain himself in front of רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question, not an attack. It gives רב אויא the chance to state his reason openly.

keyTerms.meaning: master, a respectful way of saying 'you'

phrases.english: He (Abaye) said to him (Rav Avya):

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אֲתָא מָר לְפִרְקָא?
phrases.english: Why did the master not come to the lecture?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אֲתָא מָר לְפִרְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins אביי's effort to calm רב יוסף.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason רב אויא missed the lecture.

steps.title: He was too weak to come
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא answers that his heart was weak and he could not come.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Because my heart was weak and I was not able to come.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא gives his reason: he felt faint and was physically unable to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Weakness from not eating is the reason. This opens the next question: why not just eat something?

keyTerms.meaning: my heart was weak, I felt faint

phrases.english: He said to him:
Because my heart was weak and I was not able.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּהֲוָה חֲלִישׁ לִבַּאי וְלָא מָצֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He was too weak to come.

steps.title: Why not eat something and come
steps.stepSummary: אביי pushes back: you could have eaten a little and then come.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Why didn't you taste something and then come?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the excuse. Weakness from hunger has an easy fix: eat something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the problem was only hunger, the excuse seems weak. רב אויא will need to explain why he could not eat.

keyTerms.meaning: you tasted something, you ate a little

phrases.english: He said to him:
Why didn't you taste something and come?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי לָא טְעַמְתְּ מִידֵּי וַאֲתֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hunger-weakness can be fixed by eating, so it does not explain the absence.

steps.title: רב הונא forbids eating before מוסף
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא answers that רב הונא forbids eating anything before davening מוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Doesn't the master hold of רב הונא's teaching? רב הונא said: A person may not taste anything before he davens מוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא defends himself with רב הונא's rule: no eating before מוסף. So he could not eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lecture came before מוסף, so according to רב הונא, eating was not allowed. That explains why he stayed weak and stayed home.

keyTerms.meaning: doesn't the master hold this view?

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּרַב הוּנָא?
phrases.english: Doesn't the master hold of this teaching of Rav Huna?
For Rav Huna said:
A person is forbidden to taste anything
before he prays the Musaf prayer!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Cites a halachic rule that blocked the easy fix.
steps.terutzMaskana: Eating before מוסף is forbidden according to רב הונא.

steps.title: Daven מוסף alone first, then eat
steps.stepSummary: אביי says he should have davened מוסף by himself, eaten, and then come.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The master should have davened מוסף alone, eaten something, and come.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a way around רב הונא's rule: daven מוסף privately first, and then eating is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא only forbids eating before מוסף. Once you have davened, even alone, the problem is gone.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The master should have
prayed the Musaf prayer alone,
and tasted something and come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבְּעִי לֵיהּ לְמָר לְצַלּוֹיֵי צְלוֹתָא דְּמוּסָפִין בְּיָחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the defense of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב הונא's rule kept him from eating.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Davening מוסף privately first would have allowed him to eat.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: don't daven before the congregation
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא answers with רבי יוחנן's rule that a person may not daven before the צבור does.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Doesn't the master hold of רבי יוחנן's teaching? A person may not daven his own תפלה before the צבור's תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא defends himself again. He could not daven alone early because רבי יוחנן forbids davening before the צבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both paths seem blocked. He could not eat before מוסף, and he could not daven מוסף before the צבור. So he had no choice but to stay weak.

keyTerms.meaning: that he should put first, go ahead of

phrases.english: He said to him:
And doesn't the master hold
of this that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A person is forbidden to put his prayer ahead
of the congregation's prayer?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר לְהָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Cites a second halachic rule that blocks the suggested fix.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He could have davened מוסף alone first.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יוחנן, davening before the צבור is forbidden.

steps.title: רבי אבא limits the rule to one who is with a צבור
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רבי אבא said רבי יוחנן's rule applies only to someone who is together with the צבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Wasn't it said about this that רבי אבא said: They taught it about someone who is with the צבור?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down רב אויא's last defense. רבי יוחנן's rule does not apply to someone home alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן only forbids davening early when you are with the צבור. רב אויא was home, so he could have davened alone, eaten, and come. Still, the story has done its job: everyone now sees he stayed home for a sincere reason, not out of disrespect.

keyTerms.meaning: they taught it about one in a congregation

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: no eating before מוסף. רבי יוחנן: don't daven before the צבור. רבי אבא: that only applies when you are with the צבור.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Wasn't it said about this
Rabbi Abba said: They taught it about one with a congregation.
phrases.notes: So someone home alone, like רב אויא, may daven before the צבור does.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אִתְּמַר עֲלַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּצִבּוּר שָׁנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense of step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits רבי יוחנן's rule to one who is with a צבור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב אויא was alone, so the rule did not apply to him.

steps.title: The הלכה follows neither רב הונא nor רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is not like רב הונא (no eating before מוסף), and not like רבי יהושע בן לוי (no eating once מנחה time arrives).
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is not like רב הונא and not like רבי יהושע בן לוי. Not like רב הונא, in the rule we just quoted. Not like רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said: Once the time for מנחה has come, a person may not taste anything before he davens מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final ruling. Both rules against eating before davening are rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's rule is the one from the story. רבי יהושע בן לוי adds a similar rule about מנחה. The גמרא rejects both, so eating a little before מוסף or before מנחה is not forbidden by these rules.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה does not follow רב הונא on eating before מוסף, and does not follow רבי יהושע בן לוי on eating before מנחה.
steps.confusionAlert: In the story, both רב אויא and אביי seemed to accept רב הונא's rule. אביי never argued with it; he only suggested davening מוסף first. Even so, the final הלכה rejects רב הונא's rule.

phrases.english: And the halacha is not like Rav Huna
and not like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
Like Rav Huna — this that we said.
phrases.notes: That's רב הונא's rule from the story: no eating before מוסף.

phrases.english: Like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi —
for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Once the time of the Mincha prayer has arrived,
a person is forbidden to taste anything
before he prays the Mincha prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵית הִלְכְתָא לָא כְּרַב הוּנָא וְלָא כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final הלכה on the rule raised in the story.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling: these rules do not forbid eating a little before מוסף or before מנחה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows neither רב הונא's rule about מוסף nor רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule about מנחה.

steps.title: רבי נחוניא בן הקנה's short prayer in the בית המדרש
steps.stepSummary: The משנה reports that רבי נחוניא בן הקנה said a short prayer when entering and when leaving the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי נחוניא בן הקנה would say a short prayer when he entered the בית המדרש and when he left.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes a personal practice of רבי נחוניא בן הקנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not one of the fixed daily תפלות. It is an extra short prayer tied to entering and leaving the place of learning.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה, the start of a new משנה

phrases.english: Mishnah:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה הָיָה מִתְפַּלֵּל
phrases.english: Rabbi Nechunya ben Hakana would pray
upon entering the study hall and upon leaving
a short prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה הָיָה מִתְפַּלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי נחוניא בן הקנה said a short prayer when entering and when leaving the בית המדרש.

steps.title: Why a prayer for the study hall?
steps.stepSummary: People ask him what the point of this prayer is.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: What place is there for this prayer?
steps.whatsHappening: People ask רבי נחוניא why he needs a special prayer for the בית המדרש. This sets up his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes a place of learning is not a place that needs a special prayer. The answer will show what can go wrong there.

keyTerms.meaning: what place is there, what is the point of

phrases.english: They said to him:
What place is there for this prayer?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה מָקוֹם לִתְפִלָּה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the practice described in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for a prayer when entering and leaving the בית המדרש.

steps.title: Praying for no mistakes and giving thanks
steps.stepSummary: He explains: on entering he prays not to cause a mistake, and on leaving he thanks ה׳ for his portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: When I enter, I pray that no mishap should happen through me. When I leave, I give thanks for my portion.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחוניא explains both parts of his prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The danger in the בית המדרש is spiritual: ruling wrongly and causing others to stumble. On leaving, he thanks ה׳ that his lot is to sit and learn תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: a mishap, an error that makes others stumble
my portion, my lot in life

phrases.english: He said to them:
Upon my entering, I pray

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יֶאֱרַע דְּבַר תַּקָּלָה עַל יָדִי.
phrases.english: that no mishap should happen through me.

phrases.aramaic: וּבִיצִיאָתִי אֲנִי נוֹתֵן הוֹדָאָה עַל חֶלְקִי.
phrases.english: And upon my leaving, I give thanks for my portion.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּכְנִיסָתִי אֲנִי מִתְפַּלֵּל שֶׁלֹּא יֶאֱרַע דְּבַר תַּקָּלָה עַל יָדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On entering he prays not to cause an error. On leaving he thanks ה׳ for his portion.

steps.title: The full words of the entering prayer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives the full text of the prayer for entering the בית המדרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The Rabbis taught: On entering, what does he say? "May it be Your will, ה׳ my God, that no mishap happen through me, that I not stumble in a matter of הלכה, and that my friends be happy with me. May I not call impure pure, or pure impure. May my friends not stumble in a matter of הלכה, and may I be happy with them."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא. It spells out the exact words of רבי נחוניא's prayer on entering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא fills in what the משנה only summarized as 'no mishap.' It names the specific fears: ruling wrongly on טמא and טהור, and either he or his friends stumbling in הלכה. It also asks that they all be glad in one another's success.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא, the start of the גמרא's discussion
I will stumble, make a mistake

steps.whatToRemember: The entering prayer asks not to err in הלכה, not to cause others to err, and for mutual joy among study partners.

phrases.english: Gemara:
The Rabbis taught:
Upon his entering, what does he say?
"May it be Your will, ה׳ my God,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יֶאֱרַע דְּבַר תַּקָּלָה עַל יָדִי,
phrases.english: that no mishap should happen through me,
and that I not stumble in a matter of halacha,
and that my colleagues rejoice in me,
and that I not say of the impure that it is pure,
nor of the pure that it is impure.
And that my colleagues not stumble in a matter of halacha,
and that I rejoice in them."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ מַהוּ אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the exact wording of the prayer mentioned in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The entering prayer asks to avoid errors in הלכה for oneself and one's friends, and for mutual joy.

steps.title: The full text of the prayer for leaving the בית המדרש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues and gives the exact words רבי נחוניא בן הקנה said when leaving the בית המדרש. He thanks ה׳ that he spends his time learning Torah and not with idle people.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he leaves, what does he say? "I thank You, ה׳ my God, that You put my lot with those who sit in the בית המדרש, and not with those who hang around on street corners. I get up early and they get up early. I get up early for Torah, and they get up early for empty things. I work hard and they work hard. I work hard and get reward, and they work hard and get no reward. I run and they run. I run to the life of the World to Come, and they run to the pit of destruction."
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא from Step 13 now gives the second half: the prayer said on the way out of the בית המדרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 12 we learned only the idea: he thanks ה׳ for his portion. Now we get the full wording. It is built in three pairs (waking early, toiling, running). Each pair shows that both groups do the same action, but only Torah learning leads somewhere lasting.

keyTerms.meaning: People who sit idly on street corners

steps.whatToRemember: The prayer on entering asks for protection from mistakes. The prayer on leaving gives thanks for the privilege of spending one's time learning Torah.

phrases.english: Upon his leaving, what does he say?
"I give thanks before You, ה׳ my God,
that You placed my portion among those who sit in the study hall
and did not place my portion among those who sit on street corners.
phrases.notes: קרנות literally means "corners": people who just hang around wasting their time.

phrases.english: For I rise early, and they rise early.
I rise early for words of Torah,
and they rise early for empty matters.
I toil and they toil.
I toil and receive reward,
and they toil and do not receive reward.
I run and they run.
I run to the life of the World to Come
and they run to the pit of destruction."

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּיצִיאָתוֹ מַהוּ אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא from Step 13 by giving the leaving prayer after the entering prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On leaving the בית המדרש, one thanks ה׳ for placing his lot among Torah learners and not among idle people.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's students ask him for paths of life
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that when רבי אליעזר was sick, his students visited and asked him to teach them how to earn עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: When רבי אליעזר became sick, his students came in to visit him. They said to him: Our teacher, teach us ways of living so that through them we will earn the life of the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about a great sage on his sickbed. This step sets up the question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new ברייתא, not part of the prayer text. It continues the theme of Torah and eternal reward that ended the last step. The students ask for practical guidance that leads to עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Paths of life, guidelines for living
The life of the World to Come

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
When Rabbi Eliezer became ill,
his students came in to visit him.
They said to him: Our teacher,
teach us paths of life,
and we will merit through them the life of the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן כְּשֶׁחָלָה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the prayer ending with עולם הבא to a story where students ask how to earn עולם הבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical guidance leads a person to the life of the World to Come?

steps.title: רבי אליעזר gives four instructions
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers with four instructions: honor your friends, keep your children from הגיון, seat them before Torah scholars, and know before Whom you stand when you pray.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Be careful about your friends' honor. Keep your children away from הגיון. Seat them at the knees of Torah scholars. When you pray, know before Whom you are standing. Because of this you will earn the life of the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers his students' question from Step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer covers how we treat people, how we raise our children, and how we pray. The last instruction ties back to the theme of תפלה in this פרק. He ends by promising that these bring עולם הבא, which directly answers what they asked.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of thinking or study (exact meaning unclear)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's path to עולם הבא: respect for others, a proper Torah education for children, and awareness of ה׳ during תפלה.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Be careful with the honor of your fellows,
and hold back your children from הגיון,
phrases.notes: This word is hard to pin down. It's some kind of thinking or study he wanted to keep young children away from.

phrases.english: and seat them between the knees of Torah scholars,
and when you pray,
know before Whom you are standing.
And because of this
you will merit the life of the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם הִזָּהֲרוּ בִּכְבוֹד חַבְרֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' request from Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Honor your fellows, keep children from הגיון, seat them before Torah scholars, and pray with awareness of ה׳. These earn עולם הבא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי cries, and his students ask why
steps.stepSummary: A second story: when רבי יוחנן בן זכאי was sick, he began to cry when his students came in. They praised him with great titles and asked why he was crying.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוחנן בן זכאי became sick, his students came in to visit him. As soon as he saw them, he began to cry. His students said to him: "Lamp of Israel, right-hand pillar, mighty hammer," why are you crying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second, similar story about a sick sage. This step sets up the students' question, and his answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The titles show how great he was. That makes his crying surprising: if anyone should feel calm facing death, it is him. The question sets the stage for his answer.

phrases.english: And when Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai became ill,
his students came in to visit him.
As soon as he saw them,
he began to cry.
His students said to him:
"Lamp of Israel, right-hand pillar,
mighty hammer,"
why are you crying?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁחָלָה רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel sickbed story, following the same pattern as רבי אליעזר's story in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why would such a great sage cry when facing death?

steps.title: Why רבן יוחנן בן זכאי is crying
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי compares being judged by a human king with being judged by הקדוש ברוך הוא. A human king is temporary and can be appeased or bribed, and even so he would cry. Before ה׳, the eternal King, he has even more reason to cry, because he does not know whether he is going to גן עדן or גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If I were being brought before a human king, who is here today and in the grave tomorrow, I would still cry. That king's anger, his prison, and even his death sentence are not forever, and I could calm him with words or bribe him with money. Now I am being brought before the King of kings, הקדוש ברוך הוא, Who lives forever. His anger, His prison, and His death are forever, and I cannot calm Him with words or bribe Him with money. On top of that, there are two paths in front of me, one to גן עדן and one to גיהנם, and I do not know which one they are taking me on. So how can I not cry?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answers his students' question from Step 17: why is he crying? He builds a comparison from a human king to ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument moves from smaller to greater. A human judge is temporary and can be swayed, and even he would make a person cry. ה׳ is eternal and cannot be swayed, so the fear is far greater. The last line adds a second reason: he does not know where he is headed.

keyTerms.meaning: A human king, literally a king of 'flesh and blood'
The Garden of Eden, the reward of the World to Come

steps.whyThisMatters: Even the greatest צדיק of his generation did not feel sure of his own judgment. The גמרא presents this as a model of real יראת שמים.

phrases.english: He said to them:
If before a king of flesh and blood
they were leading me,
who is here today and in the grave tomorrow,
so that if he is angry with me,
his anger is not an eternal anger;
and if he imprisons me,
his imprisonment is not an eternal imprisonment;
and if he kills me,
his killing is not an eternal death;
and I am able to appease him with words
and to bribe him with money;

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי כֵן הָיִיתִי בּוֹכֶה,
phrases.english: even so, I would cry.
And now that they are leading me

phrases.aramaic: לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: before the King of the kings of kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא חַי וְקַיָּים לְעוֹלָם וּלְעוֹלְמֵי עוֹלָמִים,
phrases.english: Who lives and endures forever and for all eternity,
so that if He is angry with me,
His anger is an eternal anger;
and if He imprisons me,
His imprisonment is an eternal imprisonment;
and if He kills me,
His killing is an eternal death;
and I am not able to appease Him with words
nor to bribe Him with money.
And not only that, but
there are two paths before me,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל גַּן עֵדֶן וְאַחַת שֶׁל גֵּיהִנָּם,
phrases.english: one of the Garden of Eden and one of Gehinnom,
and I do not know on which one they are leading me;
and shall I not cry?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: אִילּוּ לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם הָיוּ מוֹלִיכִין אוֹתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' question from Step 17 about why he was crying.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is the great רבן יוחנן בן זכאי crying?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is about to face the eternal judgment of הקדוש ברוך הוא, which cannot be undone or swayed, and he does not know whether he is going to גן עדן or גיהנם.

steps.title: The students ask for a blessing
steps.stepSummary: The students ask their teacher for a ברכה. He blesses them that their fear of Heaven should be like their fear of people.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Our teacher, bless us. He said to them: May it be ה׳'s will that the fear of Heaven be upon you like the fear of flesh and blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask for a parting ברכה, and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי gives one. The wording of this ברכה sets up the students' surprised question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה sounds strange at first. We would expect fear of Heaven to be greater than fear of people, not merely equal to it. That puzzle is exactly what the students raise next.

phrases.english: They said to him: Our teacher, bless us.
He said to them:
"May it be His will that the fear of Heaven be upon you
like the fear of flesh and blood."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: רַבֵּינוּ, בָּרְכֵנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story continues: after his explanation, the students ask for a blessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His ברכה is that their fear of Heaven should equal their fear of people.

steps.title: The students ask: only that much?
steps.stepSummary: The students are surprised. Is fear of Heaven supposed to be only as much as fear of people?
steps.simpleTranslation: His students said to him: Only up to here?
steps.whatsHappening: The students question the ברכה. It seems too small to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They assume fear of ה׳ should be much greater than fear of humans. So a ברכה that only makes them equal sounds like a small goal.

keyTerms.meaning: Only up to here? Only this much?

phrases.english: His students said to him:
Only up to here?
phrases.notes: They mean: only as much as fear of people? Shouldn't fear of ה׳ be much more?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו: עַד כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the ברכה given in Step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why bless them with fear of Heaven that is only equal to fear of people, and not greater?

steps.title: If only you reached that level
steps.stepSummary: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי answers that reaching even this level would be wonderful. A person who sins worries only that no human will see him, and forgets that ה׳ sees everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If only! Know that when a person commits a sin, he says: 'I hope no person sees me.'
steps.whatsHappening: He explains why his ברכה is actually a big one. People are more careful in front of other people than in front of ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person sins, he checks whether people are watching, but not whether ה׳ is watching. If he feared ה׳ even as much as he fears people, he would never sin. So reaching this level would be a huge achievement.
steps.whatToRemember: Fear of Heaven equal to fear of people is not a small goal. Most people sin precisely because they worry about humans watching more than about ה׳ watching.

phrases.english: He said to them: If only!
Know that when a person commits a sin,
he says: "So that no person sees me."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: וּלְוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the students' surprise from Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is a blessing of fear of Heaven equal to fear of people enough?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: People hide their sins from other people but not from ה׳, so reaching even equal fear would stop a person from sinning.

steps.title: His final words before passing away
steps.stepSummary: Right before he dies, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי tells his students to take the vessels out of the room because of טומאה, and to prepare a chair for חזקיהו מלך יהודה, who is coming.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the time of his passing, he said to them: Clear out the vessels because of the impurity, and prepare a chair for חזקיהו, king of Judah, who is coming.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with his last instructions, one practical and one spiritual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First he takes care of a halachic detail: once he dies, his body will make the vessels in the room טמא. Then he says that חזקיהו מלך יהודה is coming, showing that at this moment he was connected to the next world.

keyTerms.meaning: Chizkiyahu, the righteous king of Judah

steps.whatToRemember: The two stories of sick גדולים (רבי אליעזר and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי) both teach about יראת שמים and how to earn עולם הבא.

phrases.english: At the time of his passing, he said to them:
Clear out the vessels because of the impurity,
phrases.notes: Once he dies, his body will make the things in the room טמא, so he wants them taken out first.

phrases.english: and prepare a chair
for Chizkiyahu, king of Judah, who is coming.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁעַת פְּטִירָתוֹ, אָמַר לָהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי with his final words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before dying, he arranged for the vessels to be removed because of טומאה and announced that חזקיהו מלך יהודה was coming.

steps.title: New משנה: must one say the full שמונה עשרה every day?
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה brings a three-way מחלוקת. רבן גמליאל says a person prays the full שמונה עשרה every day. רבי יהושע says a shortened version is enough. רבי עקיבא says it depends on whether the person knows the תפילה fluently.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבן גמליאל says: Every single day a person prays שמונה עשרה. רבי יהושע says: a shortened version of שמונה עשרה. רבי עקיבא says: if his תפילה flows smoothly from his mouth, he prays the full שמונה עשרה, and if not, a shortened version of שמונה עשרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The stories are over, and a new משנה begins. It asks how much of שמונה עשרה a person must say each day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three opinions. רבן גמליאל requires the full eighteen ברכות. רבי יהושע allows a shortened version. רבי עקיבא takes a middle path: someone fluent says the full version, and someone who is not fluent may say the shortened one.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה'; it marks the start of a new משנה
The prayer of eighteen ברכות, the עמידה
A shortened version of שמונה עשרה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new פרק. It is a new משנה inside the same פרק, so the topic shifts from the stories back to the laws of תפילה.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Rabban Gamliel says:
Each and every day
a person prays the eighteen [blessings].

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: מֵעֵין שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: an abridged version of the eighteen.
Rabbi Akiva says:
If his prayer is fluent in his mouth,
he prays the eighteen;
and if not, an abridged version of the eighteen.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: בְּכָל יוֹם וְיוֹם מִתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם שְׁמֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the aggadic stories end.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל requires the full שמונה עשרה daily, רבי יהושע allows a shortened version, and רבי עקיבא requires the full version only for someone fluent.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: A fixed prayer is not real pleading
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר adds his view to the משנה: someone who makes his תפילה 'fixed' is not truly asking for mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: A person who makes his prayer a fixed thing, his prayer is not a real plea for mercy.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with another opinion about תפילה. רבי אליעזר warns that a תפילה said as a 'fixed' routine is missing something important.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 was about how much of the תפילה a person must say. רבי אליעזר moves to how a person says it. The heart of תפילה is תחנונים, pleading for mercy, and a 'fixed' prayer loses that. The גמרא will later explain what 'fixed' means.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not say that having set times or a set text for תפילה is wrong. He is criticizing a certain kind of 'fixed' prayer, and the גמרא will define it later.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One who makes his prayer fixed,
his prayer is not a plea for mercy.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: הָעוֹשֶׂה תְּפִלָּתוֹ קֶבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another תנא's view to the משנה. The focus moves from how much to pray to the attitude of the prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תפילה said as a fixed routine is not considered תחנונים.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: A short prayer in a dangerous place
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע teaches that a person in a dangerous place says a short special prayer instead of the full תפילה, and he gives its exact words.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: Someone walking in a dangerous place says a short prayer: 'Save, ה׳, Your people, the remnant of Israel. At every פרשת העיבור may their needs be before You. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who listens to prayer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי יהושע's rule for someone in danger and quotes the short prayer he should say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person in a dangerous place cannot calmly say the full תפילה, so he gets a short one. The prayer asks ה׳ to save כלל ישראל and ends with the ending of the ברכה 'שומע תפילה'. The unclear phrase 'פרשת העיבור' will be explained by the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: A phrase the גמרא will explain later

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the obligation of תפילה can bend for a person's situation. In real danger, a short focused prayer takes the place of the full one.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
One who is walking in a place of danger
prays a short prayer, and says:
"Save, ה׳, Your people,
the remnant of Israel;
at every parashat ha'ibur
may their needs be before You.
Blessed are You, ה׳, Who listens to prayer."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: הַהוֹלֵךְ בִּמְקוֹם סַכָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a special case: a person whose situation stops him from saying the full תפילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a place of danger, a person says a short prayer with set wording instead of the full תפילה.

steps.title: Facing the Temple while riding or sailing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches what a traveler should do: get off the donkey, or at least turn his face, or at least point his heart toward קדשי הקדשים. Someone on a ship or raft points his heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was riding on a donkey, he should get down and pray. If he can't get down, he should turn his face. If he can't turn his face, he should point his heart toward the Holy of Holies. If he was traveling on a ship or a raft, he should point his heart toward the Holy of Holies.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a step-by-step order for a traveler who wants to pray properly: do the best you can, and if you can't, go down one level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The best way is to stand on the ground and pray calmly. If that is not possible, turning his body toward the בית המקדש is next best. The minimum is to point his heart toward קדשי הקדשים. On a ship or raft he can't control his direction, so pointing his heart is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: He should turn his face toward the Temple
He should direct his heart and thoughts
The Holy of Holies, the innermost room of the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: There is a ladder of levels for facing the בית המקדש: get down and pray, turn your face, and at the very least direct your heart toward קדשי הקדשים.

phrases.english: If he was riding on a donkey,
he should get down and pray;
and if he is not able to get down,
he should turn his face.
phrases.notes: He means turn toward the direction of the בית המקדש.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהַחֲזִיר אֶת פָּנָיו
phrases.english: And if he is not able to turn his face,
he should direct his heart
toward the Holy of Holies.
If he was traveling in a ship or on a raft,

phrases.aramaic: יְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית קׇדְשֵׁי הַקׇּדָשִׁים.
phrases.english: he should direct his heart toward the Holy of Holies.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה רוֹכֵב עַל הַחֲמוֹר יֵרֵד וְיִתְפַּלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with travelers, but moves from what to say to which direction to face while praying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A traveler gets down to pray if he can. If not, he turns his face toward the Temple. If not, he directs his heart toward קדשי הקדשים. On a ship or raft, directing the heart is enough.

steps.title: The גמרא asks what the eighteen blessings are based on
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the eighteen ברכות of שמונה עשרה correspond to.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: These eighteen blessings, what do they correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a basic question about the משנה's subject: why does שמונה עשרה have exactly eighteen ברכות? This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (step 23) spoke about praying 'שמונה עשרה' every day. The גמרא wants to know what the number eighteen is based on. Answers will follow in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
The eighteen ברכות of the עמידה

phrases.english: Gemara:
These eighteen [blessings],
what do they correspond to?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה כְּנֶגֶד מִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה has ended. The גמרא opens its discussion by going back to the first opinion in the משנה about שמונה עשרה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the eighteen ברכות of the עמידה are based on, and why there are exactly eighteen.

steps.title: Eighteen mentions of ה׳'s name in David's psalm
steps.stepSummary: רבי הלל בריה דרבי שמואל בר נחמני answers that the eighteen ברכות match the eighteen times ה׳'s name appears in the psalm הבו לה׳ בני אלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי הלל בריה דרבי שמואל בר נחמני said: The eighteen ברכות correspond to the eighteen mentions of ה׳'s name that דוד said in the psalm 'Give to ה׳, O sons of might.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the question from step 27. The eighteen ברכות match the eighteen times ה׳'s name is mentioned in one chapter of תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was where the number eighteen comes from. This answer ties the number to a psalm of praise, where דוד mentions ה׳'s name eighteen times. So each ברכה lines up with one mention of the name.

keyTerms.meaning: Opening words of the psalm in תהלים chapter 29

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי הִלֵּל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Hillel, son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani, said:
Corresponding to the eighteen mentions of ה׳'s name

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד בְּ״הָבוּ לַה׳ בְּנֵי אֵלִים״.
phrases.english: that David said in 'Give to ה׳, O sons of might.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי הִלֵּל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי כְּנֶגֶד שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה אַזְכָּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The eighteen ברכות match the eighteen mentions of ה׳'s name in הבו לה׳ בני אלים.

steps.title: Eighteen mentions of ה׳'s name in קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a different source: the eighteen mentions of ה׳'s name in קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: They correspond to the eighteen mentions of ה׳'s name in קריאת שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives another answer to the same question. He points to קריאת שמע instead of the psalm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף agrees that the number comes from mentions of ה׳'s name, but he picks a different text. קריאת שמע is closely tied to תפילה, so it is a natural model for the ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: The reading of the שמע, said morning and evening

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּנֶגֶד שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה אַזְכָּרוֹת שֶׁבִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע.
phrases.english: Corresponding to the eighteen mentions of Hashem's name in קריאת שמע.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר כְּנֶגֶד שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה אַזְכָּרוֹת שֶׁבִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The eighteen ברכות match the eighteen mentions of ה׳'s name in קריאת שמע.

steps.title: Eighteen vertebrae in the spine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי, quoted by רבי תנחום, says the eighteen ברכות match the eighteen vertebrae of the spine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: They correspond to the eighteen vertebrae in the spine.
steps.whatsHappening: A third answer is given. This time the number eighteen is tied to the human body, the bones of the spine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two answers looked to texts. This one looks to the body that stands and bows in תפילה. That link to the spine sets up the next teaching about bowing.

keyTerms.meaning: Vertebrae, the small bones of the backbone

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Tanchum said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Corresponding to the eighteen vertebrae in the spine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי כְּנֶגֶד שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה חוּלְיוֹת שֶׁבַּשִּׁדְרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The eighteen ברכות match the eighteen vertebrae of the spine.
steps.whatToRemember: Three sources for eighteen: the psalm הבו לה׳ (eighteen names), קריאת שמע (eighteen names), and the spine (eighteen vertebrae).

steps.title: Bowing until the vertebrae stick out
steps.stepSummary: Using the same chain of names, רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that one who prays must bow until all his vertebrae stick out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי תנחום said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: One who prays must bow until all the vertebrae in his spine stick out.
steps.whatsHappening: Because the last answer mentioned the spine, the גמרא brings another teaching of the same רבי about the spine. It tells us how deep a person must bow in תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a side-teaching linked by the shared topic of vertebrae. The rule sets a deep bow: the back must bend enough that each bone stands out. The next steps will offer other measures.

keyTerms.meaning: That they stick out as the back bends

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Tanchum said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
One who prays must bow
until all the vertebrae in the spine stick out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּכְרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Linked to step 30 by the shared topic of the spine's vertebrae.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who prays must bow until all his vertebrae stick out.

steps.title: Bowing until he sees an איסר opposite his heart
steps.stepSummary: עולא gives a different measure for the bow: low enough to see an איסר coin opposite his heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Until he can see an איסר coin opposite his heart.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives another way to measure how far to bow. He uses a picture of a small coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of describing the back, עולא gives a simple visual test. The person bends until a coin in front of him lines up opposite his heart.

phrases.english: Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּרְאֶה אִיסָּר כְּנֶגֶד לִבּוֹ.
phrases.english: Until he can see an איסר opposite his heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא אָמַר עַד כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּרְאֶה אִיסָּר כְּנֶגֶד לִבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different measure for the same bow described in step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One bows until he can see an איסר opposite his heart.

steps.title: A nod of the head is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא is lenient: once a person nods his head forward, he does not need to bow further.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: Once he has moved his head, he no longer needs to bow further.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives the easiest measure of all. A nod of the head counts as the bow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is much less than the deep bow of רבי יהושע בן לוי. According to רבי חנינא, the head motion alone is enough.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
Once he has moved his head
he no longer needs to bow further.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּעְנַע רֹאשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A lenient measure compared to steps 31 and 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nod of the head is enough for the bow.

steps.title: רבא limits the nod to someone for whom bowing is hard
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי חנינא's leniency applies only when bowing is painful for him and he looks like one who bows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: That is only when he is straining himself, and he looks like someone who is bowing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a limit to רבי חנינא's easy rule. A nod is enough only for someone who finds bowing hard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without רבא, we might think anyone may just nod. רבא says the nod counts only if bending is a strain for him and it still looks like a bow. Someone who can bow properly should do so.

keyTerms.meaning: He is straining or paining himself
He looks like someone who bows

phrases.english: Rava said:
But that is only when he is straining himself,
phrases.notes: He means someone for whom bending down is hard or painful.

phrases.english: and he looks like someone who is bowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא וְהוּא דִּמְצַעַר נַפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רבי חנינא's leniency from step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A nod is enough only when bowing is a strain for him and he looks like one who bows.
steps.whatToRemember: The bow: until the vertebrae stick out (רבי יהושע בן לוי), until he sees an איסר opposite his heart (עולא), or a nod (רבי חנינא), but only for someone who finds bowing hard (רבא).

steps.title: There are really nineteen ברכות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the name שמונה עשרה: the תפילה actually has nineteen ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are eighteen?! They are nineteen!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main topic and asks a sharp question: all these sources explain eighteen, but the תפילה has nineteen ברכות. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every source above explained the number eighteen. But the תפילה as we say it has nineteen ברכות, so the count does not match. The גמרא now needs to explain the extra ברכה.

phrases.english: These are eighteen?!
They are nineteen!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי תַּמְנֵי סְרֵי תְּשַׁסְרֵי הָוְויָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the bowing side-topic and returns to the count of ברכות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the תפילה has eighteen ברכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sources explain eighteen, but the תפילה as said has nineteen ברכות.

steps.title: The nineteenth ברכה was added later in יבנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי explains that ברכת המינים was instituted later in יבנה, so it was not part of the original eighteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: The blessing against the heretics was instituted in יבנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question of why we say 'eighteen' when there are nineteen ברכות. The answer is that one ברכה, ברכת המינים, was added later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original תפילה had eighteen ברכות, and that is where the name שמונה עשרה comes from. ברכת המינים was added afterward in יבנה, so the old name stayed even after the count grew to nineteen.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing against the heretics (in today's סידור, 'ולמלשינים')
The town where the Sages gathered after the Second Temple was destroyed

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:
The blessing of the heretics, they instituted it in Yavne.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: בִּרְכַּת הַמִּינִים בְּיַבְנֶה תִּקְּנוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 35 about the name שמונה עשרה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical explanation: the extra ברכה was added later
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The name שמונה עשרה seems wrong, since there are nineteen ברכות
steps.terutzMaskana: The name reflects the original eighteen; ברכת המינים was added later in יבנה

steps.title: What does the added blessing correspond to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source hints at the nineteenth ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Corresponding to what did they institute it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question that sets up the next step. Earlier it gave sources for the number eighteen, so now it wants a hint for the nineteenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the eighteen ברכות were matched to eighteen things: names of הקב״ה in a מזמור, names in קריאת שמע, and vertebrae in the spine. If the number is based on those, the added ברכה should also match something.

phrases.english: Corresponding to what did they institute it?
phrases.notes: The earlier views matched the eighteen ברכות to eighteen things. So what matches number nineteen?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּנֶגֶד מִי תִּקְּנוּהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the answer that a nineteenth ברכה was added
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What hint matches the nineteenth ברכה, according to each earlier source for eighteen

steps.title: A hint for the nineteenth blessing in each earlier source
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי gives a matching hint for the nineteenth ברכה according to each of the three earlier views.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: According to רבי הלל בריה דרבי שמואל בר נחמני, it matches 'The God of glory thunders.' According to רב יוסף, it matches the word 'One' in קריאת שמע. According to רבי תנחום in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, it matches the small vertebra in the spine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי answers the question by going through each earlier source for the number eighteen. For each one, he points to a nineteenth item that matches the added ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the מזמור, the eighteen mentions use the main name of הקב״ה, and 'אל הכבוד' is an extra, different name. For קריאת שמע, the extra is the word 'אחד'. For the spine, it is one small extra vertebra. Each earlier source turns out to have room for a nineteenth.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One', the key word in the first פסוק of שמע
A vertebra, one bone of the spine

steps.whatToRemember: All three sources for 'eighteen' also contain a hint for the nineteenth ברכה, ברכת המינים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי הִלֵּל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי:
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Hillel, son of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani:
phrases.notes: He said earlier that the eighteen ברכות match eighteen names of הקב״ה in תהלים 29.

phrases.english: It corresponds to "The God of glory thunders."
According to Rav Yosef,
it corresponds to "One" that is in the Shema.

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: According to what Rabbi Tanchum said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
it corresponds to the small vertebra in the spine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי לְרַבִּי הִלֵּל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 37
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each source has a nineteenth element: 'אל הכבוד הרעים', 'אחד' in שמע, and the small vertebra

steps.title: שמעון הפקולי arranges the eighteen ברכות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that שמעון הפקולי arranged the eighteen ברכות in order before רבן גמליאל in יבנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: שמעון הפקולי arranged the eighteen ברכות in order before רבן גמליאל in יבנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the story of ברכת המינים. It starts by telling who set the eighteen ברכות in their order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי לוי said ברכת המינים was made in יבנה, the גמרא now gives the background. In יבנה, the eighteen ברכות were arranged in order. That sets the stage for adding the new ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught, the opening of a ברייתא

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: שִׁמְעוֹן הַפָּקוֹלִי הִסְדִּיר שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה בְּרָכוֹת
phrases.english: Shimon HaPakuli arranged the eighteen blessings

phrases.aramaic: לִפְנֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל עַל הַסֵּדֶר בְּיַבְנֶה.
phrases.english: before Rabban Gamliel, in order, in Yavne.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁמְעוֹן הַפָּקוֹלִי הִסְדִּיר שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה בְּרָכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the background story for רבי לוי's statement that ברכת המינים was made in יבנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The eighteen ברכות were set in order by שמעון הפקולי before רבן גמליאל in יבנה

steps.title: שמואל הקטן composes ברכת המינים
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל asks who can compose ברכת המינים, and שמואל הקטן stands up and composes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to the Sages: Is there anyone who knows how to compose the blessing against the heretics? שמואל הקטן stood up and composed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the story. רבן גמליאל looks for someone able to write the new ברכה, and שמואל הקטן does it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows how the nineteenth ברכה actually came about. It was a new composition by שמואל הקטן, added on top of the eighteen that were already arranged.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא of the יבנה generation

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to the Sages:
Is there any person who knows
how to compose the blessing of the heretics?
Shmuel HaKatan stood up and composed it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לַחֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכת המינים was composed by שמואל הקטן at רבן גמליאל's request

steps.title: The next year he forgot it
steps.stepSummary: The story continues: a year later, שמואל הקטן forgot the ברכה he had composed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next year, he forgot it,
steps.whatsHappening: This line moves the story forward and sets up what comes next. A year later, שמואל הקטן himself forgot the ברכה he had written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sentence is not finished here. The ברייתא is about to tell us what happened after he forgot, so this is a setup line for the next part of the story.

phrases.english: The next year, he forgot it,
phrases.notes: 'He' is שמואל הקטן, and 'it' is the ברכה he composed. The sentence keeps going after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְשָׁנָה אַחֶרֶת שְׁכָחָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of שמואל הקטן and sets up the next event
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A year later, שמואל הקטן forgot ברכת המינים (the story continues)
